title: Dedicated capacity rapid triage: SLA-Stamp & profile orchestration
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Enterprise incoming requests for Dedicated (reserved) GPU capacity are increasing and our current intake rubric is slow, inconsistent, and depends heavily on engineering capacity to compute SLO/throughput recommendations. Goal: Ship a repeatable 'SLA-Stamp' triage workflow and profile orchestration that lets PMs and Solutions Engineers (SEs) produce a validated SLA profile within 48 hours of intake. Scope: non-bug product requests (new customer or quota increase). Excludes complex hybrid on-prem migrations. Deliverables: 1) decision matrix (latency/throughput/burst tolerance/data-sensitivity -> SLA band), 2) mapping from SLA band to recommended GPU class and reserved throughput range, 3) canned scaling policy templates (conservative, balanced, aggressive) for Dedicated Pools, 4) triage UI checklist for SEs, 5) automation stub for ENG that computes initial numeric recommendations based on workload fingerprints. Acceptance criteria: - Triage time average < 48h on pilot cohort of 10 customers - 80% of recommendations accepted by ENG with no rework for simple web-scale workloads - Templates cover > 85% of incoming Dedicated requests during pilot - Documentation and runbook links added to Console onboarding workflow
decision_summary: Adopt SLA-Stamp: a deterministic rubric assigning an SLA band (Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum) based on customer workload fingerprint (qps, steady throughput, burst tolerance, model family, data sensitivity).

Default GPU mapping: Bronze -> T4/RTX-class (cost-optimized), Silver -> A10/A100-40GB (balanced), Gold -> A100-80GB/H100-80GB (low-latency/large-KV), Platinum -> multi-GPU H100 pools with reserved headroom.
Introduce three scaling templates: conservative (min=1, burst=+25%), balanced (min=2, burst=+50%), aggressive (min=4, burst=+100%), with clear limits for provisioned burst credits.
Automate numeric estimates: use sample input (tokens/sec, avg seq length, convo pattern) to produce a starting reserved throughput recommendation; engineering will validate in a follow-up sizing job.
Fallback policy: when requested GPU class is unavailable, system will fall back by SLA band to a compatible model variant (quantized/ distillation) with an opt-in consent from customer.
triage_flow: 1) SE intake form captured (qps, tokens/sec, model, data sensitivity, target p95 latency, expected daily tokens).
2) SLA-Stamp scoring: computational score (throughput need), latency sensitivity score, burst tolerance score, data-sensitivity multiplier.
3) Map scores -> SLA band and GPU class suggestion; produce scaling template and initial reserved throughput range.
4) Attach initial recommendation to intake ticket and notify ENG sizing queue for validation within 48h.
5) ENG sizing either approves, tweaks (and logs rationale), or requests a pilot validation run (short test job).
6) SE closes loop with customer with the recommended SLA band, expected cost levers, and fallback options.
example_recommendation: Workload fingerprint: steady 6k tokens/sec (avg 32 tokens/req), occasional spikes to 30k tokens/sec for 10 minutes, low-latency p95 target 120ms, model: Llama-2-70B-int8, data sensitivity: internal PII.
SLA-Stamp result: Gold band (latency-sensitive, high steady throughput + burst tolerance).
Recommended GPU class: A100-80GB or H100-80GB pool (quantization-aware runtime).
Reserved throughput: 6k tokens/sec provisioned, policy: balanced scaling (min 2 nodes, burst headroom to handle spikes via pre-approved burst credits), max nodes 12.
Fallback: if H100 not available, offer quantized Llama-2-70B-int4 on A100-80GB with a performance caveat and trial run.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot cohort (10 customers) triaged end-to-end in <48h average
ENG acceptance rate >80% for numeric recommendations without rework
Pilot customers agree to proposed SLA band in >70% of cases
Documentation + Console onboarding step published and linked from runbook
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: engineering sizing inaccuracies for novel RLHF workloads -> Mitigation: require pilot smoke test and mark as 'requires pilot' in SLA-Stamp.
Risk: customers with long-tail burst patterns may exceed burst credits -> Mitigation: conservative burst caps and explicit contract language; offer burst buyups.
Risk: GPU class shortage in region -> Mitigation: automated fallback paths and cross-region migration playbook in Console.
